items.question: In one line each — what are EC2 and S3 for?
options: EC2 runs your code (compute); S3 stores files (object storage)
EC2 stores files forever; S3 runs your application code
Both are only for billing reports
Both replace IAM completely
items.ren_hint_tanglish: EC2 = code run aagum. S3 = files store aagum.
items.explanation: EC2 is rented virtual compute. S3 is durable object storage. Almost every AWS app uses both.

items.question: A developer stores user-uploaded photos on the EC2 instance's local disk. What is the risk?
options: If the instance stops, crashes, or is replaced, the photos can be lost
S3 automatically deletes them after one hour
Local disk is more durable than S3 by design
There is no risk — EC2 disk is permanent forever
items.ren_hint_english: EC2 local disk is not permanent storage for user files.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: EC2 local disk temporary — photos S3-la store pannunga.
items.explanation: Persist user files in S3. EC2 keeps the URL in the database — not the file bytes on local disk.

items.question: A team picks t3.micro for a production database because it is cheapest. Under sustained launch-day traffic, what goes wrong?
options: Burstable CPU credits run out and performance collapses under continuous load
t3.micro automatically becomes m5.large with no downtime
S3 Block Public Access turns off by itself
The VPC deletes the private subnet
items.ren_hint_english: t3 = burst credits. Production DB needs sustained CPU (e.g. m5 family).
items.ren_hint_tanglish: t3.micro burst credits — sustained production-ku wrong fit.
items.explanation: Choose instance type for steady-state production load, not development price. Burstable types are for light intermittent work.

items.situation: Food delivery app pieces: (1) Node.js backend API, (2) React static frontend files, (3) customer profile photos.
items.question: Where should each piece live?
options: API on EC2; React files and photos in S3
Everything only on one EC2 local disk
Photos on EC2; API and React only in S3 as running processes
All three must live only inside CloudWatch
items.ren_hint_english: Running code → EC2. Static/user files → S3.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: Running code = EC2. Static files + photos = S3.
items.explanation: Backend processes requests on EC2. Frontend static assets and user photos belong in S3.

items.situation: You discover an S3 bucket of customer invoices set to Public access.
items.question: What is the first action, and what does it prevent?
options: Enable Block Public Access immediately — stops public downloads even if objects look public
Leave it public and email customers later
Delete the AWS account without fixing the bucket
Move the invoices onto an EC2 local disk instead
items.ren_hint_english: Prevent first — Block Public Access is the master switch.
items.ren_hint_tanglish: First Block Public Access enable pannunga — master switch.
items.explanation: Block Public Access overrides public object settings. Then audit access logs and tighten policy so it cannot happen again.

items.situation: When a user uploads a profile photo, your app receives it on compute, then must store it so it survives any server restart.
items.question: Which service stores that photo long-term? (Type EC2 or S3)
items.ren_hint_english: Long-term files → S3. EC2 only receives then hands off.
items.explanation: EC2 may receive the upload; S3 stores it. The database holds the S3 URL.
